text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1% today to $131.83, continuing a sharp downturn that started after the stock spiked to $141.22 just three days ago on September 15th. The reversal appears tied to oil prices sliding as crude supplies prove more resilient than feared—despite ongoing Middle East tensions including Houthi attacks and Iranian threats to the Strait of Hormuz, traders are pricing in a recovery in Saudi Arabian shipments, which is pulling crude down from earlier spikes. US oil prices currently sit at $107 per barrel, down meaningfully from levels that would have supported the stock's mid-September peak.

The broader pattern here reflects how oil stocks move in lockstep with crude prices and supply expectations. Even though geopolitical risks—Iranian escalation, attacks near Saudi infrastructure, and shipping threats—remain very real and could disrupt supplies at any moment, the market is currently trading on the assumption that those risks won't fully materialize, weighing down both oil and integrated energy companies like ConocoPhillips.
